title: What should we call the beam of a torch that never stops?
description: A torch at point T shines a beam through a marked point L, and the beam goes on without an end. The starting point is found first, then the direction, and the name is written with the starting point first. Keeko's doubt, that the beam stops at the marked point, is broken by the beam that carries on past L.
teaching_notes: One idea: a ray has one starting point, goes on in one direction, and is named with the starting point first. Watch for students who think that a ray stops at the last point marked on it.

source: A torch at T shines a beam towards a lamp post L. The beam go
video_script.why: The child sees that a beam with one starting point that goes on in one direction is a ray, and that its name begins at the starting point.
video_script.substitution: Treat the torch beam as a straight mark that starts at the torch and carries on past a marked point.
video_script.anchor: a torch at point T shining a beam through a marked point L, and on without an end
video_script.wrong_answer: the beam stops at the point L
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the beam stops at the point L because L is the last point marked. The beam is shown carrying on past L, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The beam is the ray T L, with starting point T

final_answer.value: It is a ray, named TL, with starting point T
final_answer.spoken: it is a ray, named T L, with starting point T

never_show: the name ray TL before the answer beat
maths_rules: The beam starts at the torch, which is the fixed point T.
The beam passes through the marked point L and goes on in one direction without any end.
A part of a line that starts at one point and goes on endlessly in one direction is a ray.
The starting point comes first in the name, so the beam is the ray TL, and its starting point is T.
Slip: L is only a point on the beam, not its end.
video_script.design: One idea: a ray starts at one point and goes on in one direction. The torch, the point T and the marked point L stay on the board all video. The wrong idea is that the beam stops at the last point marked.
